name: How does interior framing differ for kitchens and bathrooms compared to standard walls?

mainEntity.name: How does interior framing differ for kitchens and bathrooms compared to standard walls?

acceptedAnswer.text: Framing for bathroom and kitchen remodels requires tailored rough openings and dedicated structural blocking that standard bedroom partitions do not need. Kitchen walls must include solid horizontal blocking between studs to anchor upper cabinets, heavy range hoods, and floating shelving securely. In bathrooms, framing must be precisely square and plumb to ensure clean tile and marble installations without uneven grout lines. Carpenters must also plan framing cavities around plumbing vent pipes, pocket doors, recessed shower niches, medicine cabinets, and reinforced backing for ADA grab bars or heavy glass shower enclosures.
acceptedAnswer.description: Kitchen and bath framing requires square corners for tile, exact cutouts for utilities, and heavy internal wood blocking for cabinets, vanities, and grab bars.
